This source is a PDF situation report published on the Yale Health / Yale School of Public Health (YSPH) domain, titled "MEASLES – THE AMERICAS 2025–2026," dated February 15, 2026 (file path: 2026-02). Several factors inform this advisory assessment:

1. **Institutional affiliation is credible but not authoritative for primary surveillance data.** Yale School of Public Health is a respected academic institution, but yalehealth.yale.edu is a university health services portal, not a primary public health surveillance agency (e.g., CDC, PAHO, state health departments). The YSPH VMOC (Viral and Molecular Outbreak Consortium or similar) is an academic monitoring unit — its reports synthesize and contextualize data rather than originate it. This limits its role to secondary/contextual use.

2. **Temporal mismatch is a significant concern.** The file path contains "2026-02," indicating a February 2026 publication date. The collection window is Q1 2025 (January–March 2025). While the report covers "2025–2026" and may contain retrospective Q1 2025 data, any figures presented will be retrospective summaries, not contemporaneous surveillance records. Cumulative vs. incident count confusion risk is elevated.

3. **Geographic scope is broader than required.** The title specifies "THE AMERICAS," not the United States specifically. Geographic granularity for US-only, subnational, or state-level data extraction is likely limited. Sub-national fields (subnational_location, locality) may be sparsely populated or absent.

4. **PDF format reduces machine readability.** Structured field extraction (cases_confirmed, hospitalizations, deaths, etc.) will require manual parsing. Evidence quotes must be carefully attributed to avoid conflating regional aggregates with US-specific figures.

5. **Publisher field is null.** While the domain implies YSPH authorship, the absence of an explicit publisher declaration is a provenance gap that warrants caution, particularly for a report that may be cited in downstream records.

6. **Independence is unclear.** The report likely synthesizes CDC, PAHO, and state health department data without independent data collection. Any figures extracted should be traced back to their primary source before being ingested as collection records.

7. **Screening and critic disagree flag** is present in the deterministic assessment, indicating internal scoring tension that warrants human advisory review despite the deterministic system not flagging it for human review. The LLM advisory layer recommends elevating this for a brief human check given the temporal mismatch and geographic scope concerns.

This source presents several compounding credibility concerns that warrant careful advisory review, even though the deterministic assessment did not flag it for human review.

**1. URL Date Mismatch (Critical Flag):** The canonical URL contains `/2026/04/09/` — a 2026 publication date — while the collection task targets Q1 2025 (January–March 2025). This is a significant temporal mismatch. A 2026-dated article reporting on a 2025 outbreak may be retrospective, but it may also contain updated or revised figures that do not reflect the state of knowledge during the target window. This distinction is critical for accurate time-windowed data collection and is not captured in the deterministic risk flags.

**2. Publisher Unknown:** The `publisher` field is null. While the domain `healthbeat.org` is identifiable, the absence of a named publisher organization reduces accountability and makes editorial independence difficult to assess. This compounds the `independence_unclear` and `missing_publisher` flags already raised deterministically.

# Measles tracker: Follow cases, outbreaks and vaccination rates across the U.S.

Measles case counts, which soared to a 34-year high in 2025, have increased even more so far in 2026.

* [Add NBC News to Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=nbcnews.com)

[Highly contagious measles virus costing the U.S. millions](https://www.nbcnews.com/now/video/highly-contagious-measles-virus-costing-the-u-s-millions-258561093840)

02:32

[Get more newson](https://www.nbcnews.com/watch)

[Add NBC News to Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=nbcnews.com)

By [Melinda Yao](https://www.nbcnews.com/author/melinda-yao-ncpn1312747) and [Joe Murphy](https://www.nbcnews.com/author/joe-murphy-ncpn920391)

Measles, one of the most contagious viruses in the world, is regularly infecting people in the U.S. again.

Already in 2026 more than 2,000 cases have been counted, making 2026 one of the two worst years for measles infections in the U.S. since 2000.

NBC News is continuing to track confirmed measles cases across the United States, using Centers for Disease Control and Prevention data.

Measles case counts reached a 34-year high last year, and a surge in weekly counts shows the virus is continuing to spread this year. In the second full week of the new year 296 new cases were reported. Since then case counts have been lower.

The disease epicenter at the start of the year was in South Carolina, where the CDC has confirmed 600-plus measles cases. As of late January, [more than 500 people were in quarantine and hundreds infected in the state](https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/south-carolina-measles-outbreak-surpasses-texas-vaccines-rcna256030). [State officials declared the South Carolina outbreak over](https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/south-carolina-measles-outbreak-over-nearly-1000-cases-rcna342358) in April.

The map below will be updated regularly to show year-to-date new measles case counts reported in each state and Washington, D.C.

Measles infection counts skyrocketed last year with 2,288 confirmed cases, the most reported since 1991. This comes despite the virus being marked as being “eliminated” in the U.S. —a designation meaning it is no longer constantly circulating — in 2000. [The U.S. is in danger of losing that status following a year of continuous spread of the disease](https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/measles-spread-year-elimination-status-rcna255008).

[Three people, including two young girls, died in the U.S.](https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/measles-south-carolina-quarantine-utah-arizona-us-rcna248435) from measles last year.

The major outbreaks last year began with [West Texas](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/measles-outbreak-mennonites-west-texas-seminole-vaccines-rcna208284) in February. In October, a measles outbreak occurred along the [Utah and Arizona border](https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/measles-spreading-utah-arizona-outbreak-vaccines-rcna238757). In all, the CDC recorded 49 measles outbreaks in 2025, up from 16 in 2024. So far in 2026, 30 measles outbreaks have been reported.

[Childhood vaccination rates have been backsliding](https://www.nbcnews.com/specials/vaccine-divide/index.html), leaving communities vulnerable to this deadly disease.

The measles vaccine was introduced in 1963, marking a turning point for the contagious disease, which used to infect hundreds of thousands and kill thousands in the country every year.

**CORRECTION (Feb. 20, 2026, 3:57 p.m. ET):** A previous version of a graphic in this article miscalculated the relative size of this year's measles case count. As of Feb. 20, this year's case count is four times the size of 2025's at the same point in the year, and 25 times the size of 2024's at the same point, not seven times and 30 times higher.

# Situation Report #4: Measles in the Americas Region. 4 June 2026

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [Download](/sites/default/files/2026/06/paho-measles-sitrep4.pdf "Situation Report #4: Measles in the Americas Region. 4 June 2026") | Between epidemiological week (EW) 1 and EW 21 of 2026 (ending on 30 May 2026), the Region of the Americas reported **21,431** confirmed measles cases from 17 countries and territories, including **31** deaths, representing a 234% increase compared to the same period in 2025. Mexico (11,184), Guatemala (6,655), the United States (1,983) and Canada (1,042) accounted for the majority (97%) of confirmed cases.  During EW 19 and EW 20 of 2026, the Region of the Americas reported **1,040** new confirmed measles cases across nine countries and territories, representing a 16.2% decrease compared with the previous two-week period (EW17-18; 1,343 new cases). This decline was driven primarily by sustained reductions in the United Stated and continued decreases in Canada and Mexico. Peru was the main exception, with cases continuing to increase during this period, mostly concentrated in Puno. Trends in Guatemala should be interpreted with caution, given possible reporting delays or updates in recent weeks2.  The outbreak continues to disproportionately affect young children, with the highest incidence rates observed among infants under one year of age. Approximately 85% of confirmed cases are either unvaccinated or have an unknown vaccination status. The D8 genotype, DSId 9171 has been identified across multiple countries and remains the main genotype detected in the Region.  Model-based estimates of transmission as of EW 21 indicate continued declines in Mexico and Canada, sustained increases in Peru, and stabilizing dynamics in the United States, with the effective reproduction number (Rₜ) near 1. Full estimates and four-week forecasts are presented in **Table 3**. Nevertheless, sustained transmission could still occur through gradual, drop-by-drop spread, underscoring the need to continue strengthening vaccination efforts. |
